NKE.rationale: Nike is in the midst of a severe fundamental deterioration with no credible near-term re-rating catalyst. Q3 FY2026 (Feb 2026) showed EPS of $0.35, down 35% YoY from $0.54, with operating income collapsing to $650M from $844M. Operating cash flow fell 76% YoY to $430M. The trajectory is sharply negative: EPS has declined from $0.78 (Q2 FY2025) to $0.53 to $0.49 to $0.35 over the last four reported quarters, a consistent deterioration. Gross margin is under severe pressure from $1.5B in annualized tariff costs, with Vietnam and Indonesia accounting for 79% of footwear production. Greater China is guided down ~20% in Q4. The stock trades at 26.9x trailing P/E on a rapidly declining earnings base — if Q4 EPS comes in at the expected $0.11, the forward P/E on depressed FY2027 estimates (~$1.85) is still ~22x, hardly cheap for a company losing share to On (+40%), Hoka (+24%), and New Balance (+19%). News sentiment is deeply negative (mean -0.38 over 90 days). The June 30 earnings report is a downside catalyst: consensus expects $0.11 EPS (down 21% YoY), and Needham warns management may signal a slow start to FY2027. The CFO transition adds execution uncertainty. The stock has fallen 22.8% in the last quarter alone, hitting near 52-week lows, yet the fundamental picture continues to worsen. This is a deteriorating business with compressed margins, shrinking China, rising competition, and tariff headwinds — all while still trading at a premium multiple.
